chronicle.text: Vaiko tied wood and wood together with fiber and was left with something that floats and carries someone across water: the first raft.
Gairel went back to what they had left in one spot a third time, to see it happen again: the first deliberate testing.
Voshe gathered food that had grown where seeds had been dropped: the first harvest from seed left in the ground.
Meinis survived an attack by wolves.
Voshe tied fiber and fiber together with fiber and was left with something to carry things in: the first carrier.
Voshe buried seed on purpose, having seen it come back as food: the beginning of farming.
Nezi scratched a mark </^\> into the ground.
Gairel came back for food left 33 weeks before, and it was still there.
Noseir drank from the sea and it did not quench their thirst.
Gairel struck flint with stone and stared at what happened.
Gairel struck flint with stone and was left with a sharp edge: the first blade.
3 people now tell that a bear mauled Meinis. It was wolves. The story changed as it was passed on.
Gairel set food aside on purpose, having found it there when it was needed before: the beginning of keeping stores.
Seshail tied flint and wood together with fiber and was left with something heavy on a handle: the first club.
At (2, 18) the heap of things people had left grew big enough to keep out a fifth of the winter cold: the first dwelling. Zeikoshe had put in the most.
Voshe struck flint where dry things lay, and they caught: the first fire made by people.
Vekem tied a bundle they had tied and a blade together with fiber and was left with a sharp point on a long shaft: the first spear.
Keiheis tied a club and fiber together with fiber and was left with something warm to wear: the first wrap.
Kunatair found that what Gego had told them was wrong, and trusted them less for it.
3 people now take the mark <v//> to go with shelter, and have for two years. Nobody decided this; it grew from where the mark was made and seen.
Seshail took in the orphan Niloga, no relation, the first time a stranger raised another's child.
A thirsty year: 3 people died for want of water.
